Definition: to be (causatively, make, pronounce or observe as) clean (ceremonially or morally)
KeyPassages: Genesis 2:3; Exodus 19:10; Exodus 20:8; Leviticus 20:7; Joshua 3:5; 1 Kings 9:3
BiblicalUsage: To make holy is one of the great verbs of the Bible: God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, the people were told to sanctify themselves before meeting God at Sinai, the Sabbath is to be kept holy, Israel is commanded to sanctify themselves and be holy because the LORD is holy, Joshua told the people to sanctify themselves because the LORD would do wonders. God said He had hallowed the house Solomon built, to put His name there for ever.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe holiness is not a quality we manufacture, it is what happens when God sets something apart for Himself, and then the set-apart thing must live like it belongs to Him. That is why the command is always the same: be ye holy, for I am holy, and I take that as the centre of the whole Bible.
